27-2005.title: Duties of owner.
27-2005.body: The owner has responsibility for keeping the premises in good repair, safe and fit for human habitation. Building maintenance and repair obligations apply to multiple dwellings.

27-2029.title: Minimum temperature to be maintained.
27-2029.body: Apartment heating requirements concern indoor temperature during heat season, October through May. Landlords provide heat subject to daytime, nighttime and outside cold weather conditions.

27-2031.title: Hot water supply.
27-2031.body: Hot water facilities supply water to bathrooms and kitchens. Water temperature and availability are distinct from space heating.

27-2047.title: Mail service.
27-2047.body: The owner arranges distribution of mail to occupants of a multiple dwelling.

27-2009.title: Bedding.
27-2009.body: The maintenance of bedding and linen involves cleanliness and sanitation.

27-2053.title: Janitorial services.
27-2053.body: A janitor performs cleaning tasks for shared building facilities.

78.title: Repairs.
78.body: Every part of a multiple dwelling must be kept in good repair. The owner has a duty to maintain the building and its facilities; tenant responsibilities are separately qualified.

80.title: Cleanliness.
80.body: Multiple dwellings and their grounds are maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

79.title: Heating.
79.body: Heating facilities in multiple dwellings concern minimum temperatures and building equipment.

81.title: Receptacles for waste matter.
81.body: Waste receptacles must be maintained and emptied.

77.title: Plumbing.
77.body: Plumbing fixtures and drainage require appropriate installation.

711.title: Grounds where landlord-tenant relationship exists.
711.body: Summary proceedings include a tenant continuing in possession after a lease term and a tenant defaulting in payment of rent. Nonpayment, written rent demand and holdover grounds have statutory qualifications.

713.title: Grounds where no landlord-tenant relationship exists.
713.body: Special circumstances allow a proceeding where there is no tenancy relationship.

721.title: Person who may maintain proceeding.
721.body: Identifies who may bring a summary proceeding.

753.title: Stay in premises occupied for dwelling purposes.
753.body: A stay of removal concerns possession of dwelling premises.

1052.title: Fees of surveyor.
1052.body: Surveying work may involve fees and necessary expenses.

210.title: Short title.
210.body: Article 6-A is the Good Cause Eviction Law.

211.title: Definitions.
211.body: Defined terms for Good Cause Eviction include landlord, tenant and housing accommodation. Article 6-A begins with definitions that explain these terms.

212.title: Local option.
212.body: Local adoption affects application of Article 6-A.

213.title: Applicability.
213.body: The applicability provision describes the statutory scope.

214.title: Covered housing accommodations.
214.body: Units covered under Article 6-A are subject to coverage conditions and exemptions.

216.title: Enforcement.
216.body: Enforcement of the Good Cause Eviction Law concerns judicial remedies.

231-c.title: Good Cause Eviction Law notice.
231-c.body: A landlord disclosure informs the tenant about Article 6-A coverage and applicability. The required notice provides notification concerning good cause protections.
